title: Affordable housing, renovictions and vacant home tax
subtitle: Also: opposition to Bill 60 tenant changes, a Normandy Drive project, paramedic safety and a committee chair appointment.
overview: Council moved several affordable housing measures forward. Staff will draft a rental renovation by-law and a rental replacement by-law for Council approval by June 30, 2026. Staff will also draft a complaint-based vacant home tax by-law at a four per cent rate. Both depend on funding in the 2026 budget update. Staff said the vacant home tax would come back to Council before the end of the second quarter of 2026. These votes were unanimous {{vote:m10}} {{vote:m13}}.

Council also opposed parts of the province's Bill 60 that weaken tenant protections {{vote:m14}}. It endorsed building affordable housing on City-owned land at 5 Normandy Drive and 7 Eastview Road, funded entirely through the Housing Accelerator Fund {{vote:m17}}. A neighbouring resident's family raised concerns about the Normandy Drive plan. Staff said the project still needs a minor variance through the Committee of Adjustment and building permits, which give the public more chances to comment.

Council also backed a call for stronger Criminal Code protections for paramedics and first responders {{vote:m5}}, and appointed Councillor Busuttil as chair or vice-chair of the Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee {{vote:m18}}.

decisions.detail: Staff are directed to draft a rental renovation by-law and a rental replacement by-law for Council approval by June 30, 2026, with $640 thousand from the Affordable Housing reserve in the 2026 budget update.
Staff are directed to draft a complaint-based vacant home tax by-law with a four per cent rate, subject to $275,000 in expenditures and estimated revenues in the 2026 budget update.
Staff will keep advocating for consistent Residential Tenancies Act changes on renovictions and report to Council on any impacts if changes occur.
Council opposes Schedule 12 of Bill 60, asks the province to proclaim Bill 97, and urges it to consider the City's regulatory registry submission.
Council endorsed an expanded City role in delivering affordable housing and option three for 5 Normandy Drive and 7 Eastview Road, with the $3,406,150 budget funded from the Housing Accelerator Fund.

Council asked the federal government to extend Criminal Code protections and tougher penalties to paramedics and other first responders, and to share the resolution with other governments and municipal associations.

decisions.item: Joint Social Services and Land Ambulance Committee chair
decisions.detail: Councillor Busuttil was appointed chair or vice-chair for a term ending November 15, 2026, or until a successor is appointed.

debate: A delegate for a community group supported the four per cent vacant home tax. The delegate suggested a lower rate for owners who self-declare, a three-year rather than two-year exemption for estate situations, public education, and a one-year pilot with a review.

One councillor worried that homeowners would end vacancy quickly to qualify for exemptions, leaving administrative costs without matching revenue. Staff said a pilot would lack the force of a full program, that the revenue estimate is an assumption, and that they would report back annually.

Several councillors pressed for public engagement on the vacant home tax by-law. Staff agreed to a light-touch effort, such as a Have Your Say survey, but would not commit to town halls. Staff will also consider the estate exemption period and water-use data when drafting.

Moving the renovation by-law timeline up meant deferring work on green development standards, roughly six months by staff's estimate. Staff said Bill 60 had already changed that work, and one councillor supported the change reluctantly.

A delegate on the Normandy Drive project said neighbours were not consulted and recalled being told years earlier that the lot could not be built on. Staff said the site is zoned low-density residential, the concept is preliminary, and it needs a minor variance and building permits.
